auxiliary_material: The paper provides mechanistic insights linking clinical response to microbial engraftment, noting that responders and long-term survivors showed enrichment of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-produ taxa (e.g., Blautia, Roseburia, Faecalibacterium) and glycan-modifying enzymes. It also suggests that mild FMT-specific gastrointestinal toxicity may serve as a marker for successful microbial integration and immune priming. Additionally, the text contrasts these findings with historical RCT data (e.g., KEYNOTE-006, CheckMate 067) to contextualize the magnitude of observed benefits, though it acknowledges limitations regarding patient selection bias.
outline_action: Search for completed Phase III randomized controlled trials involving FMT or defined microbiome consortia combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Verify completion status and primary outcome data for these specific high-level trials.
remaining_gap: The gap requires confirmation of completed large-scale Phase III randomized controlled trials. This study is a Phase I single-arm trial, not a Phase III RCT. While it mentions a planned Phase II randomized trial (ME.17), it does not provide data on any completed Phase III trials confirming efficacy.
useful_material: This study reports results from the MIMic trial, a multicenter, single-arm Phase I safety trial evaluating oral FMT combined with anti-PD1 therapy in 20 patients with advanced melanoma. The study found that the combination was safe and associated with an objective response rate (ORR) of 65%, median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 29.6 months, and median overall survival (mOS) of 52.8 months. These outcomes were compared favorably to historical randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of anti-PD1 monotherapy. The authors explicitly state that the sample size was small, there was no control arm, and the results are hypothesis-generating. The study identifies a subsequent randomized Phase II Canadian study (ME.17, NCT06623461) designed to evaluate the potential benefit of this intervention.
